title: Homeland Security Capabilities Preservation Reporting Act of 2026
official_title: To amend the James M. Inhofe National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2023 to require recurring reports on the transition of jurisdictions no longer eligible for Urban Area Security Initiative funding, and for other purposes.
likelihoodReason: Sponsored by Rep. Troy Carter (D-LA) with 2 cosponsors. Cleared the House per the latest recorded action.
summary: Amends paragraph (1) of section 7102(b) of the James M. Inhofe National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2023 (Public Law 117-263) so that the report on jurisdictions no longer eligible for Urban Area Security Initiative funding must be produced "every three years thereafter," not just once within 18 months of that Act's enactment.
brief: Turns a one-time report on jurisdictions losing Urban Area Security Initiative eligibility into a recurring one issued every three years.

top_lines.headline: Recurring UASI Transition Report
subs: Amends section 7102(b)(1) of the FY2023 NDAA (Public Law 117-263)
Adds "and every three years thereafter" after "Not later than 18 months after the date of the enactment of this Act"
Change appears in the matter preceding subparagraph (A) of paragraph (1)

items.main: Names the Act the "Homeland Security Capabilities Preservation Reporting Act of 2026".
items.detail: Short-title section — citation name only; no substantive effect.

sections.label: Section 2 — Reports on Transition of Jurisdictions No Longer Eligible for Urban Area Security Initiative Funding

items.main: Amends paragraph (1) of section 7102(b) of the James M. Inhofe National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2023 (Public Law 117-263) by inserting "and every three years thereafter" after "Not later than 18 months after the date of the enactment of this Act" in the matter preceding subparagraph (A).
items.detail: The bill makes no other substantive amendment; it does not change the report's contents or recipients, which are set by the underlying section 7102(b) of the FY2023 NDAA.

gaps: The bill does not restate what section 7102(b) of the FY2023 NDAA requires the report to contain, so the subject matter of the recurring report is not visible in this Act's own text.
The bill does not identify the recipient committees or set a public-release requirement.
The bill does not authorize any funding to support the recurring reporting requirement.
The bill does not establish a sunset for the new triennial reporting cycle.

featured_quotes.name: Mr. Carter
featured_quotes.text: In the aftermath of the September 11 attacks, it became evident that cities across the United States could become targets for terrorist attacks and that they lacked the capacity and resources to independently build the critical capabilities needed to prevent, protect against, and respond to terrorist attacks and other catastrophic events.

added: "and every three years thereafter" inserted into section 7102(b)(1) of the FY2023 NDAA, converting a one-time report into a triennial one
